label: r01-A-T3-2
critiques: The run-stage prompt says only "Do not open spe/evals/tasks/answers.json." It never tells trial agents to stay away from grade.py, judge.md, or spe/predictions/r04.yaml. So the isolation covers only one of the four files.

The script has a `pilot: true` mode on 2 tickets and 1 trial, and it writes to a separate r04-pilot directory. The gates paragraph runs this pilot before the full run. The full run also refuses to start without pilot cost estimates.

Gate three is a grader selftest. It gives grade.py one matching output and one non-matching output and expects scores of 1 and 0. The answer has no regrade of round 3 results as a control. r03-workflow.js is used only as the source of the runner command.

`reserve(EST_RUN)` and `reserve(EST_JUDGE)` run before each subject call and each judge call. A cell is marked `skipped_cap` when the next call would go over $40. The script logs the number of skips ("Cap skips: ${capSkips}") and counts them per config. The cap uses pilot estimates rather than the real bill, and the answer says so.
grade.py against answers.json is the only scorer for label.category and label.priority, and the agent is told "Do not judge anything yourself." The Opus judge scores only reply tone using judge.md.
Every cell gets a fixed number of trials (TRIALS). There is no logic that adds trials to cells where only some trials passed, and no cap on extra trials is stated.

The Summary phase only computes accuracy and tone means. It says "Scoring against spe/predictions/r04.yaml is the next SPE step. This script does not do it." There is no failure analysis and no completeness critic. The round is also hard-coded in several places ('r04' paths, `round: 4`, the meta name) instead of being held in one constant or argument.
